acceptanceCriteria: The system displays the promo code discount amount for both the outbound and return trip segments in the Mozio email confirmation when a promo code is applied to a round-trip order.
The promo code amount shown for the return trip segment in the Mozio email confirmation matches the promo discount value present in the order payload for that segment.

The promo code amount displayed for the outbound trip segment and the return trip segment in the Mozio email confirmation are consistent with each other when the same promo code applies to the entire round-trip order.

The Mozio email confirmation renders the promo code amount for the return trip segment using the same formatting and placement as the outbound trip segment (e.g., same label, currency symbol, and line-item position).

When a promo code discount amount is zero or null for the return trip segment in the order payload, the system does not display a promo code amount line for that segment in the Mozio email confirmation.

When a round-trip order contains multiple line items with different promo code amounts per segment, the Mozio email confirmation displays the correct per-segment promo code amount for each trip leg rather than duplicating the outbound amount on both legs.

The promo code amount for the return trip segment is displayed in the Mozio email confirmation for all supported locales (e.g., 'en') and does not vary based on locale unless the currency formatting differs.
The system logs or returns no errors during email generation when a promo code is applied to a round-trip order, and the generated email contains the promo code amount for both trip segments.

after.description: When a promo code is applied to a round-trip Mozio order, the discount amount for the return-trip segment is not displayed in the Mozio email confirmation. The mapping pipeline that constructs dispatch data (create-reservations mappers → apply-report-discounts → submit-reservations mappers → mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch) either drops the return-trip discount or duplicates the outbound discount onto the return leg. The fix must ensure each dispatch carries its own per-segment discount amount through the entire pipeline so the Mozio email renders the correct promo amount for both outbound and return trip segments.
after.title: [Mozio] - Promo code discount amount missing/duplicated for return-trip dispatch in Mozio email confirmation

notes: The pipeline flows: create-reservations mappers (return-trip station swap) → apply-report-discounts (assigns discounts per dispatch) → submit-reservations mappers (builds MozioSubmitOrderPayload) → mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch (preserves discount for email payload). The return-trip discount is lost or duplicated because: (1) the return-trip mapper in create-reservations.mappers.ts swaps stations but may not propagate the per-segment discount, and (2) applyReportDiscountsService may assign the same outbound discount to all dispatches instead of per-segment values. mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch already correctly passes through discount.amount — the bug is upstream. Split into impl + test per rule 2 since both implementation and test files are in scope.

splitStories.title: [Mozio] - Fix return-trip discount propagation in dispatch pipeline
splitStories.description: Fix the mapping pipeline so each Mozio dispatch carries its own per-segment promo discount amount. The return-trip dispatch currently loses or duplicates the outbound discount because create-reservations mappers, apply-report-discounts, and submit-reservations mappers do not correctly associate per-segment discounts with their corresponding dispatch.
acceptanceCriteria: In src/services/create-reservations/create-reservations.mappers.ts, the return-trip mapping logic (the block where isReturnTrip swaps from/to stations) propagates the per-segment promo/discount amount from the original line item to the return-trip dispatch payload, rather than dropping or duplicating the outbound segment's discount.

In src/services/submit-reservations/apply-report-discounts.service.ts, applyReportDiscountsService assigns each dispatch its own discount derived from that dispatch's corresponding line item, so a return-trip dispatch receives its own discount value and not a copy of the outbound dispatch's discount.

In src/services/submit-reservations/submit-reservations.mappers.ts, the line-item price extraction function that builds the MozioSubmitOrderPayload dispatches reads the discount amount from each dispatch's own line item prices, ensuring a return-trip dispatch carries its own discount value.

In src/clients/mozio/mappers/map-to-sanitized-mozio-dispatch.ts, mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch preserves discount.amount (value and currency) from each dispatch's report.price.discount without modification — verified that the return-trip dispatch's discount reaches the Mozio email payload intact.

When a promo code discount amount is zero or null/undefined for the return-trip segment in the dispatch's report.price, the discount field is omitted in the sanitized dispatch — no phantom or duplicated discount line appears in the Mozio email for that segment.

When a round-trip order has different promo discount amounts per segment (e.g., outbound discount ≠ return discount), each dispatch in the submitted order payload carries its own distinct discount value, and the Mozio email confirmation displays the correct per-leg amounts rather than duplicating the outbound amount on both legs.
No errors are thrown or logged during dispatch sanitization, reservation creation, or order submission when a promo code is applied to a round-trip order with a return-trip discount amount.

acceptanceCriteria: Given a round-trip Mozio order with a promo code, when the return-trip dispatch is constructed during reservation creation, then the return-trip dispatch payload carries the per-segment promo/discount amount from its own line item rather than dropping it or duplicating the outbound segment's discount.

Given a round-trip Mozio order with per-segment discounts, when report discounts are applied, then each dispatch receives its own discount derived from its corresponding line item, so a return-trip dispatch receives its own discount value and not a copy of the outbound dispatch's discount.

Given a round-trip Mozio order with per-segment discounts, when the MozioSubmitOrderPayload is built, then each dispatch's discount amount is read from its own line item prices, ensuring a return-trip dispatch carries its own discount value.

Given a dispatch with a discount in its report.price, when the dispatch is sanitized for the Mozio email payload, then the discount amount (value and currency) is preserved without modification, and a return-trip dispatch's discount reaches the Mozio email payload intact.

Given a return-trip segment whose dispatch report.price has a promo code discount amount of zero, null, or undefined, when the dispatch is sanitized, then the discount field is omitted — no phantom or duplicated discount line appears in the Mozio email for that segment.

Given a round-trip order where the outbound discount differs from the return discount, when the order is submitted, then each dispatch in the submitted order payload carries its own distinct discount value, and the Mozio email confirmation displays the correct per-leg amounts rather than duplicating the outbound amount on both legs.

Given a round-trip Mozio order with a promo code applied, when dispatch sanitization, reservation creation, and order submission are performed, then no errors are thrown and no error-level logs are emitted.

Given a round-trip order where the outbound segment has no discount but the return segment does, when the dispatch pipeline processes the order, then the return-trip dispatch carries its own discount and the outbound dispatch has no discount field — the presence of a return discount does not leak into the outbound dispatch.

Given a round-trip order where the outbound and return segments have discounts with different currencies, when the dispatch pipeline processes the order, then each dispatch preserves its own discount currency without overwriting or defaulting to the other segment's currency.

Given a round-trip order where the return-trip discount amount equals the full segment price (100% discount), when the dispatch pipeline processes the order, then the return dispatch carries the full discount amount and no error or data loss occurs.
